title: All agree: no keeping of the precepts in the way ordered to salvation without special grace
source_text: VII. Porro Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae communi consensu agnoscunt neminem absque specialis gratiae auxilio posse praecepta divina observare, vel in totum, vel in parte, quoad modum illum quo ad vitam & salutem aeternam ordinantur: nempe, ita ut observatio ista sit aliquid quod ejus salutem per se promoveat, & gratiam vel gloriam ipsi promereatur.
pass_a_gloss: VII. Further the Doctors of the Roman Church acknowledge by common consent that no one without the help of special grace can observe the divine precepts, either in whole or in part, as to that mode by which they are ordered to life and eternal salvation: namely, so that that observance be something which of itself promotes his salvation, and merits grace or glory for him.
pass_b_english: The doctors of the Roman Church agree that without the help of special grace no one can keep God's precepts, wholly or in part, in the way that orders them to life and eternal salvation. That is, no one can keep them so that the keeping of itself advances his salvation and merits grace or glory for him.

lemmas.latin: vel in totum, vel in parte
lemmas.gloss: either in whole or in part
merits grace or glory for him

choices.why: Grace given for a particular act, distinguished from God's general concurrence with all causes; 'help' keeps the scholastic auxilium.
